summary: Specifies updated procedures for handling Broadcast, Unknown Unicast, or Multicast (BUM) traffic in Ethernet VPNs, including selective multicast and segmentation of provider tunnels. It updates RFC 7432.

eli5.summary: Some messages must reach many receivers, like a school announcement. This updates how virtual private networks deliver such announcements efficiently.

questions: what is an s-pmsi a-d route
subtitle: Fills the gaps in how Ethernet VPNs deliver broadcast and multicast traffic, with selective and segmented tunnels.

tldr.problem: RFC 7432 defines how Ethernet VPNs handle Broadcast, Unknown Unicast and Multicast (BUM) traffic, but leaves gaps around selective tunnels and tunnel segmentation across ASes and regions.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 9572 reuses the VPLS and MVPN procedures with EVPN-specific differences, and adds three EVPN route types: Per-Region I-PMSI A-D (9), S-PMSI A-D (10) and Leaf A-D (11).
tldr.outcome: EVPN operators can send multicast only to interested PEs and can split provider tunnels at AS or region borders. The document updates RFC 7432.

today: RFC 9572 is a Proposed Standard published in May 2024 that updates RFC 7432. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Filling the Gaps in EVPN BUM Handling
sections.content:
RFC 7432 specifies BGP MPLS-based Ethernet VPN (EVPN), including how it handles Broadcast, Unknown Unicast or Multicast (BUM) traffic. For details it points to RFC 7117 (multicast in VPLS) but leaves a few feature gaps around selective tunnels and tunnel segmentation. RFC 9572 fills those gaps.

Instead of repeating text, it only specifies the differences from the procedures in RFC 7117 and RFC 7524. These differences apply to EVPNs only and are not updates to those two RFCs.

MVPN, VPLS and EVPN all need to discover the other Provider Edges (PEs) and announce inclusive tunnels. The document uses I-PMSI (Inclusive P-Multicast Service Interface) as the shared concept. EVPN announces it with Inclusive Multicast Ethernet Tag (IMET) A-D routes. For selective tunnels all three use the term Selective PMSI (S-PMSI) A-D routes.
sections.eli5: Some VPN messages have to go to many places at once. This RFC fills in missing rules for doing that smartly.

sections.title: Why Segment Provider Tunnels
sections.content:
A provider tunnel that carries BUM or multicast traffic can be cut into segments for technical or administrative reasons. Different providers may use different tunnel technologies, such as ingress replication, RSVP-TE P2MP or Multipoint LDP (mLDP), and even with the same technology it may be impractical to set up a tunnel across a provider boundary. The ASBRs then stitch the segments together.

Segmentation can also divide one AS or area into smaller regions. Instead of ingress-replicating to 100 PEs in the whole AS, a PE only replicates to local PEs and Area Border Routers, which replicate further. This reduces both the forwarding burden and the leaf-tracking burden in the control plane. Smaller regions also make tunnel aggregation more bandwidth efficient and allow smaller BIER subdomains.

RFC 7524 assumes segmentation happens at area borders. RFC 9572 extends this to regions, where a region may be a sub-area or an entire AS plus its external links. For EVPNs the inter-AS procedures follow those of MVPNs, so all ASBRs can re-advertise their best route and each becomes the root of its own intra-AS segment.
sections.eli5: Instead of one huge speaker shouting to the whole country, each town gets its own speaker, and the towns pass the message along.

sections.title: Three New EVPN Route Types
sections.content:
RFC 7432, RFC 9136 and RFC 9251 define eight EVPN route types. This document adds three more. The first two start with a Type 1 Route Distinguisher whose Administrator sub-field MUST match that of the other current EVPN routes, other than Leaf A-D routes, from the same router for the same EVPN instance.

  • Per-Region I-PMSI A-D (type 9): an RD (8 octets), an Ethernet Tag ID (4 octets) and a Region ID (8 octets) encoded like an extended community.
  • S-PMSI A-D (type 10): the same as the RFC 7117 route plus an Ethernet Tag ID and an Originator's Addr Length field, with source, group and originator address fields. The procedures of RFC 7117 apply, including wildcards, but at per-Ethernet-Tag granularity.
  • Leaf A-D (type 11): a Route Key, which is the NLRI of the route being answered, plus the originator's address (4 or 16 octets).

A Leaf A-D route is originated in response to a PMSI route such as an IMET, per-region I-PMSI or S-PMSI A-D route.
sections.eli5: BGP gets three new kinds of notes: one saying a whole region offers a shared tunnel, one for tunnels about certain streams, and one saying I want to join.

sections.title: Selective Multicast
sections.content:
RFC 9251 already lets EVPN do selective forwarding of IP multicast with SMET routes, but it assumes selective forwarding is used for every flow with ingress replication. An operator may not want to track every (C-S,C-G) or (C-*,C-G) state, and may need selective forwarding only for a few high-rate flows. For that case, and for tunnel types other than ingress replication or BIER, the S-PMSI and Leaf A-D procedures of RFC 7117 are used.

In short, a source NVE advertises S-PMSI A-D routes to announce the tunnels used for certain flows. Receiving NVEs either join the announced PIM or mLDP tunnel, or answer with Leaf A-D routes when the L flag is set in the PMSI Tunnel Attribute (PTA), so that the source can include them as leaves.

One optimization is allowed. If an egress NVE has already advertised a corresponding SMET route, it MAY omit the Leaf A-D route, and the source NVE MUST use the SMET route instead. The optional optimizations of RFC 8534 also apply.
sections.eli5: Most announcements go to every room, but a few busy ones are sent only to rooms that signed up. Rooms can sign up with a short note.

sections.title: Inter-AS Segmentation Procedures
sections.content:
For EVPNs, RFC 9572 does not use the VPLS rule that elects a single ASBR per AS. Each ASBR re-advertises the Inter-AS A-D route to its IBGP peers and roots its own intra-AS segment, and the segments are disjoint. The PTA MUST specify the tunnel for the segment. The ASBR sets the L flag to 1 only if it needs to know the leaves to build the tunnel, and must be configured with an import RT to accept Leaf A-D routes.

Leaf tracking. An ingress PE does not set the L flag in its IMET A-D routes. It MUST find the leaves in its AS from the BGP next hops in the IMET A-D routes it receives. PEs in the same AS have different next hops, while PEs in other ASes appear with the address of an ASBR, so only those ASBRs count as leaves. With ingress replication, an ASBR MUST advertise the same label for the same Ethernet Tag ID and EVI, and a PE MUST add routes with the same (nexthop, label) tuple as a single branch in its flooding list.

Backward compatibility. Legacy PEs would treat remote-AS PEs as leaves. To handle them, upgraded PEs set a flag bit in the EVPN Multicast Flags Extended Community, per-PE I-PMSI routes stay inside the local AS, and ASBRs originate per-region I-PMSI A-D routes toward external peers. One ASBR is elected to serve legacy PEs using the Designated Forwarder (DF) Election EC of RFC 8584, with the AC-DF bit cleared.
sections.eli5: Each border gate relays the announcement into its own town and counts only the gates, not every house, as receivers. Old-style houses get help from one chosen gate.

sections.title: Inter-Region Segmentation and Multihoming
sections.content:
If an ASBR does not support segmentation, the provider tunnels in a neighboring AS can run across the external link. A region can then be an entire AS plus that link, defined as a BGP peer group rather than automatically from IGP areas. The border routers become Regional Border Routers (RBRs), the replacement for ABRs, and may set up multihop EBGP sessions with route reflectors or PEs in the neighboring AS.

To avoid propagating every PE's route everywhere, the I-PMSI routes of all PEs in a region can be aggregated into one per-region I-PMSI route originated by the RBRs. There are no per-region S-PMSI routes, since few PEs advertise S-PMSI routes for the same source and group. A Region ID can encode an AS number or area ID, using a Source AS extended community of sub-type 0x09 for AS numbers.

Unlike RFC 7524, RBRs change the BGP next hop when they re-advertise I/S-PMSI A-D routes and do not use the S-NH-EC, so ingress and egress PEs need not understand it. A downstream PE or RBR that originates a Leaf A-D route builds an IP-based Route Target from the received Next Hop, and the upstream RBR configures a matching RT, so RFC 4684 constrained distribution can be used.

For multihoming, Ethernet Segment Identifier (ESI) labels SHOULD be allocated from a Domain-wide Common Block (DCB, RFC 9573) for all tunnel types. Not using DCB-allocated ESI labels is outside the scope of the document.
sections.eli5: A region is a group of towns that share one speaker. Border officers announce for the whole group, and tell neighbors to send replies to their address.

sections.title: IANA Allocations
sections.content:
IANA assigned the new EVPN route types 9 (Per-Region I-PMSI A-D route), 10 (S-PMSI A-D route) and 11 (Leaf A-D route) in the EVPN Route Types registry.

It also assigned bit 8, named Segmentation Support, in the Multicast Flags Extended Community registry created by RFC 9251. Upgraded PEs use the flag to show they support the new procedures.
sections.eli5: IANA wrote the three new route kinds and one new flag in its official lists.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The selective forwarding procedures here are based on the same procedures as MVPN (RFC 6513, RFC 6514) and VPLS multicast (RFC 7117). The segmentation procedures are based on those for MVPN inter-AS segmentation, inter-area segmentation (RFC 7524) and VPLS multicast inter-AS segmentation.

Applied to EVPNs, they do not introduce new security concerns beyond those discussed in those documents, and none compared to RFC 7432.
sections.eli5: Because it copies methods already used elsewhere, it brings no new kinds of danger.
